title: Sudden desyncs after clearing one song
body:
It doesn't look like an issue to me at first, but i think it's intentional as of (1.3.0). This scenario occurs to any charts either official or custom chart.

1. Play any song.
2. After you clear once, it temporarily freezes the game and the console writes it for you. Afterwards it resumes, thus Don-chan's full combo announcement gets delayed.
author: sakurada0291

comments.body: This is indeed intentional, the sudden freeze is actually the game saving(it can also happen when leaving song select, starting a song, or selecting some filters), and its probably the best option we have rn, the save needs to be delayed, because while the game is saving, TekaTeka is doing some shenanigans with the save related data, and if you enter song select while that, the game crashes(leading to the most common crash that used to happen before 1.3.0 or beta 1.2.3)
I was on my way to record one song for the showcase and it just paused directly afterwards...

title: Gauge does not gain in Diverge Note chart in Taiko Mode
body: The mentioned case only applies to any custom charts that have diverge notes (譜面分岐) except Normal branch[?] where Professional and Master branch does not gain gauge during gameplay.
author: sakurada0291

comments.body: Does this happens on Shin-uchi mode or both normal and Shin-uchi?

The problem is in the multiplier computation ported over from Python.

The code looks like this:

fumen.header.b460_b463_normal_professional_ratio = \
            int(65536 * (total_notes['normal'] / total_notes['professional']))

In Python, the parenthesized part might look like (3/4) and comes out as a float .75, which gets multiplied by 65536 to yield 49152.0, which is cast back to an int 49152.

In C#, parenthesizing like that gets

(3/4) = 0 * 65536 = 0 => no score progression.

Fix is to move the parents to be around the (65536 * total_notes['normal']) / total_notes['professional']

I have a patch for this, just not near my machine for the next few days to send it. :(

Edit: note that if the number of notes in the professional/master branch happens to be equal to the notes in the normal branch, the fraction will resolve to 1 and scoring would continue to work. In the more likely case that the number of notes in the other branch is greater than the number of notes in normal, the fraction will be 0 and break scoring.

> Does this happens on Shin-uchi mode or both normal and Shin-uchi?

Re: Both of them.

Edit: it gains in Normal and Professional except Master. My bad.
Will wait for the devs to review my wording if it's good enough. These are subject to edit if there are mistakes.

title: Fix issue where some songs don't start with correct offset
body: If a song has a #BPMCHANGE command prior to the first measure, that value is used instead of the BPM value for determining audio start delay.

Can you explain why you think it would break old songs?

The old ultramix had both the original songs and the new songs in the musicinfo, lets say the both had the UID `11`, if you use `GetModPath(11)` it will search for any mods containing a song with a UID of 11, not original songs, so, despite being on the original game, it will add it to the list of songs, so there will be 2 songs with the same UID and same ID, this obviously will break things(just like it happens when a new taiko pass song with the same ID as one from ultramix gets released). Plus, letting a mod override a original song is a big no no for me

title: Modifications to make the ModdedSongsManager handle reloads
body:
This splits the construction of the manager into two parts. The first part does the one-time load of the mods in TekaSongs, handling Fumen and TJA songs. The second part, called "publishing" handles the process of making the mods available to the music data of the game. This needs to be called at startup and whenever a Reload() occurs, which is handled with a postfix patch.

Manager functionality that was repeated in both the TJA and Fumen mods was consolidated into a single method.

Tested this change with and without the SwapSongLanguages, verifying that both Fumen and TJA mods were present, and that the SwapSongLanguages mod worked as expected.
author: bionyx187
